newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico execs say peso strength "not worrisome".
newsitem.headline: Mexico execs say peso strength "not worrisome".

text.p: Mexico's most powerful group of financial executives, countering speculation that the peso was overvalued, said on Thursday its strength reflects "a higher level of confidence in economic policy."

The Mexican Institute of Finance Executives said a number of factors, including this year's $2.245 billion in debt issues, a debt pre-payment to the U.S. Treasury and a sustained increase in international reserves to $8.8 billion, have attracted foreign capital to stabilize the currency.

"The actual exchange rate is a faithful reflection of the actual economic conditions and the evolution of principal macroeconomic variables, reasons which we do not consider at all worrisome," the group said.
A seasonal decline in economic activity at the beginning of each year has also helped reduce dollar demand in the exchange markets and promoted stability, it added.
However, the group said the exchange rate cannot appreciate indefinitely.
The benchmark 24-hour peso contract strengthened 0.8 centavos Thursday to close between 7.7535 and 7.7560 to the dollar.
